title: Close the remaining store-data fail-opens that switch the whole write guard off
action: The sfg-3 judge passed the fix and then found the SAME defect class still live, one call frame from the code just hardened. This cell closes the rest of it. (1) heartbeat_stale (hooks/write_guard/store.rs:374-375) does `date_parse_ms(session.get("last_heartbeat"))?`. It is reached from checks.rs:354 inside check_workspace_ownership, which checks.rs:555 propagates, so a malformed last_heartbeat in the WORKSPACE OWNER's session record (not the acting session's) yields Err(Nd) -> check_write Err -> Outcome::Delegate -> hooks/mod.rs emit_undecidable -> exit 0, "The guard did NOT run on it". The same reader is `?`d again at store.rs:391 inside is_concurrent_mode. (2) checks.rs:145 does `control_root_for_state(control_root)?`, which returns Err(Nd) on CtxOutcome::Threw (store.rs:270), and check_product_root_silent (store.rs:105/107) returns Err(Nd) for a non-string product_root or a configured product_root directory that does not exist — so config store data can switch the whole guard off the same way. Decide the honest read for each — a stamp the reader cannot parse should read the SAFE way for that call site (a heartbeat it cannot parse is not evidence of staleness; a product_root it cannot resolve is not evidence of containment) — and make each reader infallible by signature, exactly as sfg-3 did for the claim readers, so no store-data parse failure can ever reach emit_undecidable. Where a genuinely undecidable input must still stop the guard, it must REFUSE (deny), never fall open. Sweep the whole write_guard module for any remaining `?` on a store or config READ that can reach resolve_write_record or check_write, and close each one; name in the commit body any you deliberately left and why. Prove red-first: a test per fixed reader that the guard still DECIDES (never Delegate/undecidable) on malformed data, failing before the fix.

truths: A malformed last_heartbeat in the workspace owner's session record NEVER makes the write guard report undecidable — the guard still runs and still decides.
A malformed last_heartbeat is read the SAFE way for its call site, and the code says which way that is and why.
A non-string or non-existent product_root NEVER makes the write guard report undecidable.
No `?` on a store or config READ inside the write_guard module can still reach emit_undecidable; any deliberately left is named in the commit body with its reason.
Where an input is genuinely undecidable, the guard REFUSES rather than falling open.
Every truth sfg-1 and sfg-3 proved still holds; all thirteen sfg1_*/sfg3_* tests still pass untouched.
Each fixed reader has a test proving the guard still decides on malformed data, and each was red before the fix.

acceptance: No malformed session, claim, cell, lane or config record can switch the write guard off; every remaining escape is either closed or named with a reason; the write_guard suite is green.

checks.evidence: store.rs:429 heartbeat_stale(&Map, f64) -> bool has no error path. All three in-module call sites close doors: checks.rs:361 sets live=true -> Ownership::Blocked -> the write-policy Deny; store.rs:446 in is_concurrent_mode, whose consumers gate on !other_live_session so true REMOVES exemptions; store.rs:469 in active_worker_session_ids, where more live workers means more denial. HUNT (fail-CLOSED hazard, not a FAIL): an unparseable last_heartbeat reads live FOREVER with no time-based self-heal, so a bad owner record can lock every other session out of a checkout until status is closed/dead or the file is repaired. HUNT (documentation defect introduced by this diff): hook_local.rs:763-767 and 836-841 still assert an unparseable heartbeat reads as false and fails OPEN, which is now the opposite of the code.

store.rs:293 control_root_for_state(&str) -> String covers Threw with root.to_string(); the fallback is the caller's own control_root, so it can never pick up another project's lane record. The worst degraded resolution is source "default", which keeps the intake gate and the workspace-ownership deny in front of the session. Before the diff the same inputs produced emit_undecidable, so any decided answer is strictly less permissive.

No live caller of check_product_root_silent remains; both former call sites keep read_config(...)? and discarded only the verdict. The corrupt-config warning still comes from read_config -> state.rs:168-170 warn_corrupt_json. No write_guard test asserted a product_root warning.

The sweep missed the lease and hold readers, same defect class, still live: check_write -> checks.rs:466 find_session_conflicts? -> store.rs:836 list_active_reservations? -> store.rs:823 lease_record_expired? -> store.rs:811 date_parse_ms? -> Err(Nd). list_path_lease_records (store.rs:723-751) does not validate expires_at/acquired_at, so a lease carrying a non-RFC3339 or numeric stamp escapes to emit_undecidable. Same class at store.rs:824 lease_to_reservation, checks.rs:500 find_foreign_holds -> store.rs:932, checks.rs:484 hold_expiry -> store.rs:960-962, checks.rs:518/530 foreign_hold_expiry -> store.rs:969, checks.rs:637 find_conflicts, and paths.rs:452 inside resolve_live_worker_count. reservation_store_corrupt and holds_store_corrupt do not gate these.

is_concurrent_mode(strict=true) is indeed only reached from main.rs:427, not through check_write. But main.rs:427 sits in the hook's own R<..> path, so Err(Nd) still reaches emit_undecidable, and shared_candidates is pushed on the Edit/Write branch too (main.rs:397-405), so every Edit/Write with a resolvable target enters that loop. One zero-byte or truncated .bee/sessions/<id>.json makes store.rs:346 return Err via read_session_strict and the whole guard falls open on a real write. Mitigating: the branch is named at store.rs:332-334, and its honest close is a DENY whose Node-parity wording this port cannot reproduce, so the remedy needs a wording decision.

git show b98f03ab --numstat reports 138 additions and 0 deletions in tests.rs, so no prior test was touched; all 8 sfg1_* and 5 sfg3_* tests ran green. cargo test --release write_guard = 218 passed, 0 failed, including the 4 new sfg4_* tests.

Each new test drives an input that pre-diff produced Err(Nd) -> Delegate, which expect_done panics on: the five unparseable heartbeat values through the old !heartbeat_stale(..)? at checks.rs and store.rs:469, the non-string and non-existent product_root through the deleted check_product_root_silent, and a .git file pointing nowhere through the old Threw -> Err(Nd) arm. All four also assert a decided verdict, so they pin that the fix decides rather than merely stops erroring.
